title: KL Before and After Mixing: A Round-Complexity Separation in Parallel Sampling
why_read: A dense theoretical paper on information-theoretic bounds for parallel sampling algorithms, of narrow interest to specialists in sampling theory or diffusion model acceleration research.
analysis: This paper studies how the number of 'rounds' needed in parallel sampling schemes depends on which of two closely related divergence measures (KL divergence averaged over schedules vs. divergence of the averaged output) is used to judge sampling quality. It proves a sharp mathematical separation showing these two criteria can require very different round counts, illustrated with a concrete combinatorial example involving balanced binary strings. This kind of result could matter for designing faster parallel sampling algorithms used in things like diffusion models, but the paper is highly technical and abstract with no direct empirical implementation. It is really aimed at theoreticians working on sampling complexity rather than general practitioners.
